ai.definition: Agentic Workflow Orchestration is a cognitive architecture that leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to create autonomous workflows. These workflows involve iterative processes where LLMs plan tasks, execute them, and self-correct based on feedback or outcomes.
ai.howItWorks: The technology implements reflection patterns and tool-use loops to transition from zero-shot capabilities to iterative refinement. This allows the LLMs to continuously improve their output through a cycle of planning, execution, and correction.
ai.problemSolved: It addresses the challenge of creating autonomous systems that can handle complex tasks without human intervention by enabling LLMs to learn from their actions and adapt accordingly.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing is not directly involved as this technology focuses on software development and cognitive architectures rather than physical products.
ai.buildProcess: The build process involves developing and training LLMs, integrating them with execution tools, and setting up feedback loops for continuous improvement. This includes defining the workflow structure, selecting appropriate LLM models, and designing the interaction between the model and external systems.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the development costs of training large language models, computational resources required for running these models, and the integration with existing tools and systems.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook suggests that this technology is moving from research to early adoption in specific domains like autonomous software engineering and advanced research.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks are still evolving for AI technologies. There may be concerns around data privacy, bias, and accountability which could require compliance with existing regulations or the development of new ones.
ai.risks: Risks include potential biases in training data, lack of transparency in decision-making processes, and ethical considerations related to autonomous systems making decisions without human oversight.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain as it depends on market adoption and specific use cases. Early adopters in high-value industries like software development or research could see significant benefits.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include more advanced reflection patterns, better integration with a wider range of tools and systems, and enhanced ethical considerations to ensure responsible AI use.

glossary.def: Cycles of self-assessment and improvement in AI systems
Iterative processes where LLMs use external tools to execute tasks and learn from the outcomes

subsystems.name: Orchestrator
subsystems.role: runs the iterative loop, deciding when to plan, act, reflect, or stop.

subsystems.name: Language model
subsystems.role: the reasoning engine that generates plans, actions, and critiques.

subsystems.name: Tool interface
subsystems.role: lets the agent call external functions, APIs, or code interpreters.

subsystems.name: Memory
subsystems.role: stores context and past steps so the agent can refer back and learn within a session.

subsystems.name: Critic
subsystems.role: assesses output quality and triggers refinement or replanning.

subsystems.name: Execution sandbox
subsystems.role: provides a safe environment for running generated code or taking actions.

buildSteps.title: Define the task and success criteria
buildSteps.detail: Specify what the agent must accomplish, how success is measured, and any constraints on time, cost, or safety.

buildSteps.title: Set up the language model interface
buildSteps.detail: Choose a model, configure API access, and design prompt templates for planning, acting, and reflecting.

buildSteps.title: Implement the tool layer
buildSteps.detail: Define each tool with a clear schema, write wrappers that call it safely, and parse its output back into the loop.

buildSteps.title: Build the orchestration loop
buildSteps.detail: Code a state machine that alternates between planning, tool use, observation, and reflection, with a clear stopping condition.

buildSteps.title: Add memory and context management
buildSteps.detail: Implement a short-term buffer and a long-term store, with retrieval that keeps the active prompt within the model's token limit.

buildSteps.title: Integrate a critic or verifier
buildSteps.detail: Add self-evaluation steps — using the same model or separate checks — that score output and trigger revisions when needed.

buildSteps.title: Create an execution sandbox
buildSteps.detail: For code or actions, provide an isolated environment with resource limits so mistakes cannot harm the host system.

buildSteps.title: Test and evaluate
buildSteps.detail: Run benchmark tasks, log full traces, measure success rate, cost, and latency, then iterate on prompts, tools, and loop logic.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models with strong reasoning
prerequisites.why: they generate plans, actions, and critiques; without them the loop has no core engine.
they let the agent interact with external systems, files, and code interpreters.
they provide long-term memory and context management beyond a single prompt window.
measuring progress and comparing architectures is still an open problem.
multi-agent systems need interoperability, but conventions are still emerging.

pathway.milestone: single-agent loops with reflection and tool use
pathway.unlocks: automating simple coding, research, and data-processing tasks.
handling complex projects that require planning, coding, and verification together.

pathway.milestone: standardised protocols for agent-tool and agent-agent interaction
pathway.unlocks: composable agent ecosystems and easier integration across platforms.

pathway.milestone: reliable, long-horizon autonomy with safety guarantees
pathway.unlocks: agents that can operate for days on open-ended goals with minimal human oversight.
